subject: Tenant data erasure journey & evidence request
messages:
From: Julia Grant <julia.grant@harborbank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Harbor Bank Security <security@harborbank.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant-level erasure — request for journey + evidence

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Harbor Bank's InfoSec team is starting our SOC 2 review and we need a clear description and artifacts showing how tenant data is erased on request. Specifically: 

- Walkthrough of the erasure journey (API request -> job completion -> verification).
- Example audit logs showing a tenant deletion event and the keys/fields that are captured.
- Time-to-complete SLA for different regions (us/eu) and large tenants.
- Any cryptographic or KMS steps that ensure residual data is not recoverable.

Can you share a concise playbook + sample artifacts we can attach to our evidence bundle? Ideally something we can consume by EOD Wednesday.

Appreciate it,
Julia
Julia Grant
Lead, Cloud Risk & Compliance
Harbor Bank
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Grant <julia.grant@harborbank.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant-level erasure — request for journey + evidence

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Dylan (runtime security) and Marissa (compliance) to provide the artifacts and a short narrative.

High-level plan we will deliver: 
1) A 2-page "Tenant Erasure Playbook" that maps the lifecycle from a customer deletion request through background job processing and audit verification.
2) Redacted sample audit logs (CSV) showing the deletion event, job id, operator id, timestamps, and final state.
3) A diagram showing cross-region replication and how TTL / tombstone propagation works (for any EU tenants we’ll note residency behavior).
4) A brief attestation letter we can sign and date for your evidence packet.

We have an internal playbook draft (attached: destruction_playbook_v1.2.pdf) — this contains the workflow, roles, and verification steps. Dylan and Marissa, can you confirm the log fields and attach an anonymized sample? Also, Julia — is a short attestation (one page) sufficient or do you need a formal notarized statement?

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: destruction_playbook_v1.2.pdf (PDF, 260KB)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant-level erasure — request for journey + evidence

Julia — attaching a redacted sample of the audit log and a diagram showing the erasure workflow. A few implementation notes below: 

- Log fields included in the sample: event_type, tenant_id (hashed), job_id, initiating_principal, initiated_at, completed_at, deleted_object_count, region, replication_state, verification_hash. (See audit_log_sample.csv attached.)
- Typical end-to-end completion time: small tenants (<=5GB) median 2–6 minutes; large tenants (100s GB) will be handled by staged background jobs — median completion ~2–6 hours depending on queued work and cross-region replication. We include TTL tombstones to prevent immediate reuse of identifiers.
- KMS: we rotate envelope keys; erasure removes object references and zeroes metadata pointers. For on-prem/private deployments we provide a separate key destruction procedure.

Attachments: audit_log_sample.csv (CSV, redacted), erasure_workflow_diagram.png (PNG)

If you need a query to extract matching events from our audit store, I can run that and provide a CSV limited to your tenant scope.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Sr. Security Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Julia Grant <julia.grant@harborbank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Harbor Bank Security <security@harborbank.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant-level erasure — request for journey + evidence

Hi Olga / Dylan — this is perfect, thank you. The playbook and the redacted logs will work for our SOC 2 bundle. A couple of quick follow-ups: 

- Can you provide a 1-page attestation we can include (signed by Redwood) that the deletion process was followed and logs reflect the described behavior?
- Please confirm that the audit logs include immutable timestamps and that the sample shows both initiated_at and completed_at for the same job_id.
- If possible, add a short note about retention windows (default TTLs) and how customers can request expedited erasure for exfil data-hold scenarios.

If you can share the attestation and a line-item confirming the timestamp immutability by EOD Thursday we'll be able to close this piece. Otherwise let's schedule 30 minutes to walk the Harbor Bank auditor through the artifacts — Tue/Wed next week are options.

Thanks again — Julia
